verdict: Bank of America's revenue rose 7% to $28.4B with net interest income up 10% to $15.8B, and net income grew 12% to $7.6B as EPS rose 18% to $0.98 — capping a year in which profit reached $30.5B.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between what the bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors and lenders — up 10% on bigger loan and deposit balances and repricing of older fixed-rate assets. The net interest yield was 2.08% (fully taxable-equivalent), up from 1.97% a year ago.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and trading: investment and brokerage fees of $5,300M (asset management fees $4,193M, up 13%), market making of $2,074M, investment banking fees of $1,666M, service charges of $1,649M, card income of $1,566M and $362M of other income.

flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — the closest thing a bank has to a cost of goods sold.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's roughly 213,000 employees — well over half of all running costs.

opex.name: Info processing & comms
opex.note: Technology, data processing and communications — the plumbing of a digital bank.

opex.name: Occupancy and equipment
opex.note: Branches, offices, ATMs and the equipment in them.

opex.name: Product delivery
opex.note: The cost of moving money: processing payments, producing cards and handling transactions.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the bank's products.

opex.name: Other operating
opex.note: Everything else — this quarter it includes higher litigation costs, partly offset by a lower FDIC special assessment accrual.

follow100Note: People are the bank's biggest cost: $37.37 of every $100 goes to pay and benefits. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Banks don't report gross profit; the chart follows BAC's own structure.
pngFooterNote: Component lines are from its Q4 2025 financial supplement.

takeaways.title: The lending engine is earning more
takeaways.text: Net interest income reached $15,750M as average loans grew 8% to $1.17 trillion and deposits topped $2 trillion, while old fixed-rate assets repriced to today's higher rates. The net interest yield widened to 2.08%, up 11 basis points from a year ago.

takeaways.title: Profit grew faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Net income rose 12% to $7,647M and EPS rose 18% to $0.98, helped by a smaller credit-loss provision ($1,308M, down from $1,452M) and an efficiency ratio that improved to 61%. For the full year, net income was $30.5B and EPS $3.81, up 19%.

takeaways.title: Capital is strong and going back to shareholders
takeaways.text: The bank returned $8.4B to shareholders ($6.3B of buybacks, $2.1B of dividends) while keeping its CET1 capital ratio at 11.4%. Net charge-offs were $1,287M — 0.44% of loans, better than 0.54% a year ago.

oneTimers: Preferred stock dividends of $328M sit between net income ($7,647M) and the $7,319M attributable to common shareholders.
4Q24 comparatives in the release reflect BAC's retrospective accounting change for certain tax-related equity investments, effective 4Q25 — year-over-year comparisons use the restated figures.
